title: A paired browser HUMAN holding ADMIN can write project.set_agent_provider, through the typed waiver arm
description:
Filed 2026-09-07 by worker-b1872f24 from parent task-969575299465484d9486ea02ff7ae336 (the Codex/provider roll-up), which is BLOCKED on this row.

MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. At HEAD ea822b90 the browser half of the provider toggle is now COMPLETE and LIVE: task-96957529 landed apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-agent-provider-offers.ts, so `/affordances/read` mints the `project.set_agent_provider` offer, `commandBuilderFor` builds a real envelope and the control is enabled. Driven end to end against a REAL daemon in the browser lane (tests/e2e/control-room/agent-provider-seats.spec.ts, 1 passed), a paired operator clicks `codex` and the daemon answers, verbatim from the rendered refusal:

    OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION
    this command requires the configured operator principal

WHY. `AGENT_PROVIDER_COMMAND_KIND` is in `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:348), and the fence at daemon-command-registry.ts:349-360 compares the authenticated principal against the daemon's CONFIGURED `operatorPrincipalId`, widening only for approvalIntent / criterion / `repository.publish` / PRODUCT_CONTRACT_ANSWER_CLARIFICATION when `isDurableHumanPrincipal` holds. A paired browser is a session-ledger HUMAN minted at pairing; it is NEVER the configured operator principal, and it cannot be — the id does not exist before pairing. So NO browser can write this setting today, however correct its caller half.

THIS IS THE task-6d5db404 SHAPE EXACTLY. That row (DONE) admitted `repository.bootstrap` for a paired browser HUMAN holding ADMIN through the typed SOFT_POLICY_WAIVER composition, after the same measurement on task-80322112's journey. The standing ruling from that escalation (mem:repository-bootstrap-browser-widening-decision-2026-09-06) is that a security-boundary widening is NEVER folded into a UI proof row; it is its own reviewed row that the UI row depends on. task-96957529 also carries a rail forbidding policy work outright, which is why its worker landed the offer and stopped here rather than greening its own e2e by widening a fence.

SCOPE: the narrowest widening already in the tree, mirroring 6d5db404 arm for arm. A paired HUMAN WITHOUT ADMIN must still get OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED. `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS`, `wiredMcpToolKinds()` and the MCP count pins stay byte-identical — the kind's trustworthiness on principal identity alone depends on it staying MCP-unreachable. The operator-credential path is unchanged. Nothing about the offer, the store, the payload roster or the wrapper's spawn resolution needs to move; they are landed and green.

WHEN THIS LANDS, ONE LINE UNPARKS THE PROOF: tests/e2e/control-room/agent-provider-seats.spec.ts asserts the refusal code today and says so in its comment. Flip it to the round trip — click codex, expect `cr.sessions.provider.recorded`, expect the `cr.sessions.provider.configured` line to come back saying codex on the panel's own 5s poll from /sessions/read. The durable write path itself is already proven live (HTTP 200 AGENT_PROVIDER_SET over the real command edge, mem:task-task-117a3cd9-handoff), so this row moves authorization only.
definitionOfDone: `project.set_agent_provider` is admitted for a paired browser HUMAN holding ADMIN through the typed SOFT_POLICY_WAIVER composition, mirroring task-6d5db404; a paired HUMAN WITHOUT ADMIN still refuses OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION, asserted by code and layer.
A drill removing the ADMIN check goes RED, recorded with the mutated path, the arm that reddened, and a SHA256-proved restore.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE THE FENCE, THE LAYER ORDER, AND THE BLAST RADIUS. No edits. Record verbatim: (a) `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src tests/e2e/control-room/` — foreign dirt noted, never reverted; (b) `sed -n '349,362p' apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts` — today's fence and its four widened kinds; (c) `grep -n 'AGENT_PROVIDER_COMMAND_KIND' apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` confirming it is in `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` and that `SETTINGS_FAMILY` gives it `CAPABILITIES.ADMIN`; (d) `sed -n '155,162p' apps/daemon/src/http/http-command-ingress.ts` — the ingress refuses `CAPABILITY_DENIED @ AUTHORIZE` BEFORE the handler, which is what makes the no-ADMIN case unreachable at the fence over HTTP; (e) `sed -n '215,228p' apps/daemon/src/planning/policy-waiver-command.ts` — the precedent's ADMIN-then-durable-human order; (f) `grep -n 'AGENT_PROVIDER_COMMAND_KIND' apps/daemon/src/daemon-v2-command-registry.ts` returning NOTHING, confirming there is no second fence to widen — if it returns anything, BOTH must move together or a hole ships. Record the HEAD sha.

WIDEN EXACTLY ONE KIND, AT ONE LINE. In `daemon-command-registry.ts`, extend the fence's widening disjunct (:356-360) with an arm that fires ONLY for `AGENT_PROVIDER_COMMAND_KIND`, and only when the principal is a durable HUMAN (`isDurableHumanPrincipal(store, principal.principalId)`) AND EXPLICITLY holds `project.admin` (read from `principal.capabilities`). The explicit ADMIN check is REQUIRED even though the ingress already enforces the capability: it is defence in depth, and it is the thing DoD 2's drill removes — without it the row's central security claim has nothing to test. A paired HUMAN missing either condition does not match the disjunct and falls through to the EXISTING refusal, which is why this shape yields `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION` with NO new code and NO new layer constant. Extend the existing comment block to say which kind was added, that it requires ADMIN where the neighbouring four do not, and that it holds only while the kind stays MCP-excluded. Do NOT add a second kind, do not touch the four existing ones, and do not alter the operator-credential path.

THE ARMS, AT THE SEAM WHERE THE FENCE ACTUALLY ANSWERS. In `daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts` — the dedicated file for this widening class — add three arms driving the registry handler DIRECTLY, not over HTTP: (1) POSITIVE: a durable HUMAN principal holding `project.admin` dispatches `project.set_agent_provider` and the command is ACCEPTED, reaching `runAgentProviderCommand`; (2) NEGATIVE, THE ONE THAT MATTERS: a durable HUMAN principal whose capabilities OMIT `project.admin` is refused `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED` at layer `DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION` — assert BOTH, per global rail 1. This arm MUST be at the handler seam: over HTTP the ingress answers `CAPABILITY_DENIED @ AUTHORIZE` first and the arm would be green without ever reaching the fence; (3) a NON-human, non-operator principal holding ADMIN is still refused the same way, so the widening turns on durable-human-ness and not on capabilities alone. Then add ONE HTTP-level arm pinning the OTHER layer explicitly — a no-ADMIN principal over the real ingress gets `CAPABILITY_DENIED @ AUTHORIZE` — so both refusing layers are named and neither can silently substitute for the other.

THE DRILL — DoD 2, and this row's central evidence. `git status --porcelain apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts` FIRST. Then delete the ADMIN check added in step 2, re-run the arms, and confirm the step-3 NEGATIVE arm goes RED — run it against the handler-seam arm, never the HTTP one, because the HTTP arm would stay green on the ingress layer and prove nothing. Record the mutated path, the exact arm that reddened with its failure line, and the restore proof. The file is TRACKED, so an empty `git diff -- apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts` after restoring is a valid proof; if any UNTRACKED file was mutated, that path needs SHA256 equality against an out-of-tree backup instead, taken in a call SEPARATE from the restore. A drill whose arm does not redden means the check is not load-bearing — stop and fix the arm rather than recording a drill that proved nothing.

PROVE MCP STAYED CLOSED — DoD 3, and it is load-bearing rather than bookkeeping: this kind is trustworthy on principal identity ALONE only while it remains MCP-unreachable. Assert BIDIRECTIONALLY per global rail 9, enumerating the served set from the dispatch seam (`wiredMcpToolKinds()`) and not only from the roster constant: `AGENT_PROVIDER_COMMAND_KIND` is in `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` AND is absent from the served kinds, asserted as set-equality rather than a subset check. Confirm every MCP roster COUNT PIN in `daemon-command-registry.test.ts` and `mcp-dispatch-port-plane.test.ts` is BYTE-IDENTICAL — `git diff` on those files must show no count literal moved. If a count did move, this row broke the exclusion and must stop, not adjust the pin.

FLIP THE BROWSER PROOF FROM REFUSAL TO ROUND TRIP — DoD 4. `tests/e2e/control-room/agent-provider-seats.spec.ts` asserts the refusal today and its comment says why; replace both the assertion AND the comment, so the file stops documenting a fence that no longer stands. Against a REAL daemon: click `codex`, expect `cr.sessions.provider.recorded` VISIBLE, expect `cr.sessions.provider.refusal` ABSENT, and expect the `cr.sessions.provider.configured` line to come back reading codex on the panel's own 5s poll from `/sessions/read`. Assert the acceptance and the configured read-back TOGETHER: a click that rendered an acceptance note without a durable write must not pass, which is the mirror of the discipline the refusal arm used (pin the code AND the unmoved configured line). Quote the spec's count line.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW. Each leg FOREGROUND and STANDALONE, read the OUTPUT not the exit code — no `Test Files N passed` line means nothing ran. Legs, quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, and the single browser spec from step 6. Repo-wide legs are a PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE: merge-base failures, HEAD failures, delta intersected with owned paths must be EMPTY; disclose foreign red verbatim, never waive it. Then read the diff as an attacker: does EXACTLY ONE kind move — `git diff` on the fence shows one added disjunct and nothing else? Can any principal that is not a durable HUMAN holding ADMIN reach the handler? Did any MCP roster count literal change? Is the operator-credential path byte-identical? Would the negative arm still redden if the ADMIN check were deleted (step 4 proved it once — confirm the restore held)? Finally, WRITE THE PROVENANCE INTO THE COMPLETION RECORD as task rail 2 requires: the owner answered a SPECIFIC security escalation with a GENERIC "unblock more tasks", taken as the nod for the narrowest shape; state that plainly rather than citing task-6d5db404 as if a human approved this kind by name, and note that `mem:repository-bootstrap-browser-widening-decision-2026-09-06` is not on disk under that name so the ruling is cited from that row's own record. comments.author: architect-6e49a205
comments.content:
PLANNING MEASUREMENT — one DoD clause cannot be satisfied where it says, and writing it there would be vacuous. HEAD, 2026-09-07.

1. THE DEFECT IS CONFIRMED. `daemon-command-registry.ts:349-360` refuses when `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS.has(kind) && principalId !== operatorPrincipalId`, widening only for approvalIntent / criterion / `repository.publish` / clarification under `isDurableHumanPrincipal`. `AGENT_PROVIDER_COMMAND_KIND` is in the set (vocabulary:348) and not in the widening list. The handler dispatches two lines later at :364 and is already landed and green. Only authorization moves.

2. **DoD 1's NEGATIVE ARM IS UNSATISFIABLE OVER HTTP — and an e2e arm written there would be green while testing nothing.** DoD 1 asks that a paired HUMAN *without* ADMIN still refuse `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION`. Measured: `http-command-ingress.ts:158-160` refuses `CAPABILITY_DENIED` at stage `AUTHORIZE` when the principal lacks the entry's `requiredCapability`, and `SETTINGS_FAMILY` (vocabulary:180) makes this kind's required capability `CAPABILITIES.ADMIN`. That gate runs at ingress, **before** the registry handler and therefore before the fence. So a no-ADMIN principal never reaches the fence and can never produce that code.

The consequence is the exact failure global rail 1 names: an arm asserting "the no-ADMIN browser was refused" goes green on the *ingress* layer and **stays green even if this row's ADMIN check is deleted outright** — which would also make DoD 2's drill fail to redden, quietly retiring the row's central security claim.

RESOLUTION IN THE PLAN: assert the no-ADMIN case at the **registry handler seam** (a direct handler call with a durable-HUMAN principal whose capabilities omit `project.admin`), where the fence really answers and where the drill reddens it — that yields exactly the code and layer DoD 1 names. Then pin the *other* layer separately: a no-ADMIN principal over the real ingress gets `CAPABILITY_DENIED @ AUTHORIZE`. Both refusing layers named, neither able to stand in for the other.

3. MIRRORING 6d5db404 IN POLICY, NOT IN MODULE SHAPE — and saying so rather than letting the divergence look like a shortcut. The `SOFT_POLICY_WAIVER` arm delegates to `policy-waiver-command.ts`, which enforces ADMIN first with its own code `POLICY_WAIVER_ADMIN_REQUIRED` at its own layer `DAEMON_POLICY_WAIVER` (:220), then durable-human (:223). That module exists because a waiver is a typed payload decision needing a witness, a one-use step-up and a ledger. Copying it here would mint a **new layer constant** (dragging in the roster-backfill rule) and make the no-ADMIN refusal a **new code** — contradicting DoD 1. `project.set_agent_provider` needs none of that ceremony.

So the chosen shape is one added disjunct in the existing fence, firing only for this kind and only when the principal is a durable HUMAN **and** explicitly holds `project.admin`. Anything missing either condition falls through to the existing refusal — no new code, no new layer, no roster movement. The explicit ADMIN check is kept even though the ingress already enforces the capability: it is defence in depth, and it is the thing DoD 2's drill removes. Without it there is nothing to drill.

4. NO SECOND FENCE TO WIDEN. `daemon-v2-command-registry.ts:138-147` has its own `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED` throw, but only for the clarification-v2 kinds; this kind is not served there. Step 1 re-confirms it, because a widened v1 beside an unwidened v2 is how a hole ships.

5. PROVENANCE (task rail 2). `mem:repository-bootstrap-browser-widening-decision-2026-09-06` is **not on disk under that name** — `read_memory` returns FileNotFoundError. The plan therefore cites the ruling from task-6d5db404's own record and requires the completion record to state plainly that the owner answered a *specific* security escalation with a *generic* "unblock more tasks", taken as the nod for the narrowest shape — not that a human approved this kind by name.
